industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, because the industry is split by the rotation itself: the AI capital-spending theme flipped from leadership to liability this week (Garran, MacroStrategy, 20-Nov; Mark Wilson, Goldman, 20-Nov; Menon, Jefferies, 26-Nov; surplus evidence in GPU rental prices cut by a third, halted shipments and banks selling AI loans), while Goldman's Jaisson (20-Nov) favours Technology among Cyclicals and Morgan Stanley (23-Nov) keeps Adyen Overweight. Relative strength D (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior). The sector rows carry the view: Semiconductors D, Hardware D (from C this week), Software B2B Enterprise C, Fintech D. Counter-case for D: the industry is the epicentre of the correction; for B: Menon says early estimate cuts bring the semiconductor bottom forward and equipment re-rates first. To D on a hyperscaler guide cut read in the sources.

sector.why: Neutral, carried: the growth data show no slowdown (US GDP 4.3%, Germany PMI 55.0) while Hatzius (Goldman, 22-Nov) sees AI weighing on the job market; relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; B prior). Pool names Alten, Nagarro, Made Tech, Reply, Sopra Steria, with Sell-side Momentum C, F, average, B and C. Counter-case: corporate budgets are the first cut if the margin rolls over. Back to D if Sell-side Momentum on the Pool names falls further.

geography.why: Overweight, from Neutral, on the row's own written condition ('to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read'): Goldman's Sharon Bell (20-Nov) argues 'Domestic not Defensive' with 2027 growth of 1.4% above consensus and the FTSE 100 at a discount with a far higher free-cash-flow yield, James Moberly (23-Nov) has growth improving through 2027 as rates peak, Marshall (22-Nov) has gilts at 4.8% by end-2027, UK core inflation is flat at 2.8% (25-Nov), and Jefferies' Duncan Farr (26-Nov) reads the Financial Policy Committee ruling as favourable for bank cost of equity. 28 Pool stocks are UK-listed and now carry a country weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum; the book holds 16.47 points UK-listed (CVS Group, Fevertree, Hilton Food, Helios Towers). Counter-case: Bell's next two quarters are 'tough', the Bank of England's decision is still unread, Oppenheimer underweights Europe as a whole, and the UK Pool names are mostly global businesses. Back to C if the Bank of England's guidance is read hawkish or a UK consumer reading arrives falling.
